claim: The world's first Passive House, a row of four homes in Darmstadt-Kranichstein, Germany, was finished in 1991; Wolfgang Feist's family was one of the four households.

(https://phai.ie/passive-house-standard/history-of-passive-house https://blog.passivehouse-international.org/kranichstein-passive-house-plus/)

claim: The Passive House Institute lists five principles: very good thermal insulation, highly energy-efficient windows, airtightness, no thermal bridges, and ventilation with heat recovery; such buildings need very little heating energy.
fact_check_evidence: Feist's iPHA interview and passive house guides describe the same ingredients: strong insulation, high-quality triple-glazed windows, an airtight envelope and heat-recovery ventilation, giving very low heating demand. (https://blog.passivehouse-international.org/first-passive-house-wolfgang-feist/ https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house)

claim: The Darmstadt pioneers had triple-glazed windows specially made for the project and fitted four ventilation units with heat recovery.
fact_check_evidence: Accounts of Kranichstein note that low-e triple glazing was not yet commercially available, so it was made for the project, and that fresh air came through heat-recovery ventilation. claim: Passive solar design uses windows, walls and floors to collect, store and distribute the sun's heat; the US Department of Energy advises windows facing within 30 degrees of true south.
fact_check_evidence: Penn State's passive solar course notes and other design guides give the same advice: collect heat through south-facing glazing and store it in the building. (https://www.e-education.psu.edu/emsc297/sites/www.e-education.psu.edu.emsc297/files/Passive%20Solar%20Design%20-%20Overhangs%20and%20Shading.pdf https://greenpassivesolar.com/passive-solar/building-characteristics/overhang-solar-control/)

claim: Passive solar design lets in the sun's low winter rays and deflects its high summer rays; roof overhangs can shade windows in summer, and thermal mass in floors and walls stores the heat.
fact_check_evidence: Penn State and Green Passive Solar explain that a fixed overhang shades high summer sun while low winter sun passes under it into the room. (https://www.e-education.psu.edu/emsc297/sites/www.e-education.psu.edu.emsc297/files/Passive%20Solar%20Design%20-%20Overhangs%20and%20Shading.pdf https://greenpassivesolar.com/passive-solar/building-characteristics/overhang-solar-control/)

claim: Curb cuts turned out to help far more than wheelchair users: parents pushing strollers, workers pushing heavy carts and travelers wheeling luggage use them too.
fact_check_evidence: 99% Invisible and Local Motion describe the curb-cut effect: features designed for disabled people that benefit strollers, bikes, carts and luggage. (https://99percentinvisible.org/episode/308-curb-cuts/ https://www.localmotion.org/the_curb_cut_effect)

claim: NC State's Center for Universal Design, founded in 1989 and guided by the architect Ronald Mace, who coined the term, defines universal design as design usable by all people, to the greatest extent possible, without the need for adaptation or specialized design.
fact_check_evidence: The Ronald L. Mace Universal Design Institute and Ireland's Centre for Excellence in Universal Design give the same definition of universal design, credited to Mace. (https://www.udinstitute.org/principles https://universaldesign.ie/about-universal-design/the-7-principles)

claim: Seven Principles of Universal Design were published in 1997; the first, Equitable Use, asks for the same means of use for all users, identical whenever possible, and avoiding segregating or stigmatizing anyone.
fact_check_evidence: Ireland's Centre for Excellence in Universal Design and the Mace Institute list the seven principles (1997, NC State), starting with Equitable Use. (https://universaldesign.ie/about-universal-design/the-7-principles https://www.udinstitute.org/principles)

claim: The 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design require ramp runs to have a running slope no steeper than 1:12, one unit of rise for every 12 of run.
fact_check_evidence: The US Access Board's guide to ramps and curb ramps gives the same 1:12 maximum running slope. (https://www.access-board.gov/ada/guides/chapter-4-ramps-and-curb-ramps/ https://www.ada.gov/resources/2010-stds-guidance/)

claim: Historic England advises starting an investigation of a building with a quick overview, identifying its functions and main phases, to see it as a functioning whole; investigation asks what it shows of its origins, form, function, date and development.
fact_check_evidence: The Archaeology Data Service and the North York Moors National Park describe Historic England's guide as the standard for investigating and recording buildings, including their form, function and development. (https://archaeologydataservice.ac.uk/library/browse/issue.xhtml?recordId=1213197&recordType=GreyLitSeries https://www.northyorkmoors.org.uk/planning/planning-advice-notes/standards-and-guidance-for-historic-building-recording)

claim: Historic England's guide lists clues to a building's phases and date: evidence of phasing such as masonry joints, architectural styles, plan elements, decorative schemes, and fixtures and fittings.
fact_check_evidence: Building recording guidance based on Historic England's standard asks recorders to identify phases of construction from structural and stylistic evidence. (https://www.abheritage.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/HBR-Levels-1.pdf https://www.northyorkmoors.org.uk/planning/planning-advice-notes/standards-and-guidance-for-historic-building-recording)

claim: Historic England's guide says plans should record structural features such as blocked doorways, windows and fireplaces, and masonry joints.
fact_check_evidence: Historic building recording guidance based on Historic England's levels asks recorders to note blocked openings and other evidence of alteration. (https://www.abheritage.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/HBR-Levels-1.pdf https://archaeologydataservice.ac.uk/library/browse/issue.xhtml?recordId=1213197&recordType=GreyLitSeries)
